name: EASI LOA M365 Licensing Mistakes Rule Pack
notes: This rule pack is designed to align with context variables already computed in Get-M365LicenseOptimizationReport.ps1.
Rules marked MANUAL are still valuable: they document what to verify and which portal/API to use.
Field 'generalCAPoliciesText' exists in the script as $generalCA but is not currently exported to CSV; you can keep it internal for rule evaluation or add it as an output column.

rules.title: User targeted by Conditional Access but missing Entra ID P1 entitlement

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — User is targeted by Conditional Access policy/policies ({generalCAPoliciesText}) but no Entra ID P1 entitlement found. Conditional Access requires Entra ID P1 for each benefiting user.
notes: If policies are tenant-wide and include the user, confirm licensing coverage across the full in-scope population.

rules.title: User targeted by risk-based Conditional Access but missing Entra ID P2 entitlement

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — User is targeted by risk-based Conditional Access policy/policies ({riskBasedCAPoliciesText}) but no Entra ID P2 (Identity Protection) entitlement found. Validate P2 coverage for in-scope users.

rules.title: PIM is in use for the user but Entra P2/Governance entitlement is missing

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — User has PIM roles (Eligible: {pimEligibleRolesText}; Active: {pimActiveRolesText}) but no Entra ID P2 entitlement found. PIM requires Entra ID P2 or Entra ID Governance for benefiting users.

rules.title: Dormant admin account (high risk) still licensed

recommendation.textTemplate: DORMANT ADMIN REVIEW — Admin roles present ({adminRolesText}) but account is dormant. Review necessity, enforce JIT/PIM where possible, and consider removing or downgrading the license if the role is no longer needed.

rules.title: Non-interactive sign-ins are recent but interactive sign-ins are stale (service/automation pattern)

recommendation.textTemplate: AUTOMATION ACCOUNT — Last interactive sign-in is old ({daysSinceSignIn} days) but non-interactive sign-in is recent ({daysSinceNonInteractiveSignIn} days). Treat as automation/service identity: validate license need and least-privilege.

rules.title: Disabled account still licensed

recommendation.textTemplate: DISABLED ACCOUNT — Account is disabled but still licensed. Consider removing the license or converting to a mailbox preservation approach if retention/hold applies.

rules.title: Deleted user still appears licensed in assignment state (needs cleanup)

recommendation.textTemplate: DELETED USER — User is deleted but licensing signals remain. Remove/cleanup license assignments and group-based licensing references.

rules.title: Guest user is licensed (validate business justification)

recommendation.textTemplate: GUEST USER — Guest account is licensed. Validate whether guest needs paid licenses or can use guest/External ID model. Remove if unjustified.

rules.title: Guest user licensed but no activity (review)

recommendation.textTemplate: GUEST ACCOUNT REVIEW — Licensed guest is dormant. Consider removing the license unless there is a contractual or operational reason to retain it.

rules.title: Account never signed in (possible provisioning/licensing error)

recommendation.textTemplate: NEVER SIGNED IN — No interactive sign-in recorded. Validate whether the account is truly used, blocked from sign-in, or missing authentication setup; remove license if unused.

rules.title: Tenant-level Entra governance prerequisites missing (manual confirmation)

recommendation.textTemplate: PREREQ GAP — Entra Governance features require prerequisite subscriptions in the tenant (AAD_PREMIUM or AAD_PREMIUM_P2). Verify tenant prerequisites and renewal status.

manualCheck: In Entra admin center: Billing > Licenses > Licensed features, confirm Governance prerequisites are present (AAD_PREMIUM or AAD_PREMIUM_P2).
If Governance SKU exists but prerequisites are missing/expired, features may not function as expected.

rules.title: Conditional Access is enabled tenant-wide without verifying per-user licensing coverage

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — Conditional Access policies are enforced tenant-wide. Validate that all benefiting users have Entra ID P1 (and P2 for risk-based policies).

rules.title: Overlapping licenses assigned (double-paying)

recommendation.textTemplate: OVERLAPPING LICENSE — Multiple suites/add-ons overlap ({overlappingSkusText}). Consolidate to a single defensible license stack per user.

rules.title: Duplicate coverage (suite + standalone add-ons)

recommendation.textTemplate: DUPLICATE COVERAGE — User holds standalone add-on(s) that are already included in their suite. Consider removing the redundant SKU(s) after validating prerequisites and dependencies.

rules.title: Direct + group licensing mixed without control (harder to govern)

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — User has mixed direct and group-based licensing. Standardize assignment to reduce drift and prevent accidental over-licensing.

rules.title: License errors present (provisioning failures)

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING ERROR — Cloud license assignment errors detected. Resolve the error state (conflicts, capacity, invalid plans) before making optimization changes.

rules.title: License capacity queue / insufficient licenses

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSE CAPACITY QUEUE — A license assignment failed due to insufficient available licenses. Purchase/add capacity or remove from other users before proceeding.

rules.title: Unknown SKU found (reference data missing)

recommendation.textTemplate: DATA GAP — SKU(s) not in pricing/reference data. Update M365SkuData.json to improve cost and optimization accuracy.

rules.title: Trial licenses left assigned (sprawl)

recommendation.textTemplate: TRIAL LICENSE — Trial SKU detected. Decide to purchase and standardize, or remove to prevent unplanned cost and drift.

rules.title: Viral/self-service licenses assigned (shadow IT)

recommendation.textTemplate: VIRAL LICENSE CLEANUP — Viral/self-service licenses detected (PowerApps/Flow). Review tenant settings and clean up unnecessary assignments.

rules.title: Shared mailbox licensed unnecessarily

recommendation.textTemplate: SHARED MAILBOX — Shared mailbox has user licensing assigned. Shared mailboxes generally do not require a license unless the mailbox exceeds 50 GB, has an active archive, or is on litigation hold. The license can typically be removed if those conditions do not apply.

rules.title: Shared mailbox exceeds 50GB without appropriate licensing

recommendation.textTemplate: SHARED MAILBOX REVIEW — Shared mailbox exceeds 50GB but is unlicensed. Assign Exchange Online Plan 2 (or qualifying suite) if the mailbox must grow beyond 50GB.

rules.title: Shared mailbox has archive enabled without the required license

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — Shared mailbox has an archive mailbox enabled but is unlicensed. Shared mailbox archiving requires Exchange Online Plan 2 or an archiving add-on depending on your SKU mix.

rules.title: Shared mailbox on litigation hold without required licensing

recommendation.textTemplate: LITIGATION HOLD — Shared mailbox is on litigation hold but is unlicensed. Ensure it has the required Exchange Online Plan 2 (or qualifying suite) for holds and compliance features.

rules.title: Room/Equipment mailbox has user license assigned (often waste)

recommendation.textTemplate: ROOM/EQUIPMENT — Room/Equipment mailbox has user licensing assigned. Validate if required (storage/holds) or remove to avoid waste.

rules.title: Mailbox storage warning (approaching quota)

recommendation.textTemplate: MAILBOX STORAGE WARNING — Mailbox is approaching quota. Consider cleanup, archive strategy, or EXO Plan 2 where justified.

rules.title: Inactive mailbox (licensed but no recent activity)

recommendation.textTemplate: INACTIVE MAILBOX — Licensed user mailbox with dormant sign-in/activity. Review retention requirements; remove license or move to appropriate mailbox preservation approach.

rules.title: Over-licensed archive (archive enabled but user has premium suite not required)

recommendation.textTemplate: OVER-LICENSED ARCHIVE — Archive needs are driving premium licensing. Validate if EXO P1 + Archiving add-on or a lower suite could satisfy requirements.

rules.title: No desktop apps detected (web-first user)

recommendation.textTemplate: RIGHTSIZE — No Office desktop apps detected. Consider plans optimized for web/mobile users if business requirements allow.

rules.title: Mobile-only usage detected (frontline pattern)

recommendation.textTemplate: RIGHTSIZE — Mobile-only usage detected. Evaluate frontline-optimized licensing after validating mailbox size, archive/hold, and desktop dependencies.

rules.title: Low Exchange usage intensity for licensed user

recommendation.textTemplate: RIGHTSIZE — Low Exchange activity intensity. Verify mailbox requirements and whether current license tier is justified.

rules.title: Teams no-desktop (web/mobile only) pattern

recommendation.textTemplate: RIGHTSIZE — Teams used without desktop client. Validate device profile and consider frontline licensing patterns when appropriate.

rules.title: Dormant account still licensed (general waste)

recommendation.textTemplate: DORMANT — User has not signed in recently ({daysSinceSignIn} days) but is licensed. Consider removing or downgrading the license after confirming retention and HR status.

rules.title: Dormant sign-in but active workload usage detected

recommendation.textTemplate: DORMANT SIGN-IN — No interactive sign-in for {daysSinceSignIn} days, however M365 workload activity (Exchange, Teams, OneDrive, or SharePoint) was detected. The account is likely active via cached credentials or mobile apps. Review sign-in hygiene but do not remove the license.

rules.title: OneDrive storage warning (approaching quota)

recommendation.textTemplate: ONEDRIVE STORAGE WARNING — Storage is approaching quota. Consider cleanup, retention policy, or higher storage entitlement where justified.

rules.title: Shelfware: licensed but no activity across key workloads

recommendation.textTemplate: SHELFWARE — License assigned but usage signals are absent or low. Consider removing or downgrading the license after confirming onboarding status and reporting data completeness.

rules.title: Frontline candidate detected (F3/F1 rationalization)

recommendation.textTemplate: FRONTLINE CANDIDATE — User appears suitable for frontline licensing. Validate blockers (archive/hold/multi-PC activations) before changing.

rules.title: Mailbox in scope of non-built-in Defender for Office 365 policies but no MDO entitlement

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — Mailbox appears in scope of Defender for Office 365 policies ({mdoPolicyCoverageText}) but no MDO entitlement found. Validate licensing for benefiting users.

rules.title: Security coverage 'None' for licensed user (baseline hardening opportunity)

recommendation.textTemplate: SECURITY GAP — User has productivity licensing but minimal security coverage. Consider baseline security (Defender/Entra) depending on risk profile and requirements.

rules.title: Compliance coverage 'None' for licensed user (baseline compliance opportunity)

recommendation.textTemplate: COMPLIANCE GAP — User has productivity licensing but minimal compliance coverage. Validate audit/retention/DLP needs; consider appropriate Purview add-ons.

rules.title: Assuming audit retention meets requirements without validating retention policies (manual)

recommendation.textTemplate: REVIEW — Validate audit retention requirements vs configured audit retention policies and user licensing.

manualCheck: In Microsoft Purview portal: Audit > Audit retention policies. Confirm retention meets business/regulatory requirements.
Default retention varies by workload; longer retention requires retention policies and appropriate user licensing.

rules.title: Using audit retention policies up to 10 years requires policy + licensing alignment (manual)

recommendation.textTemplate: PREREQ GAP — Long audit retention policies (up to 10 years) require premium audit capabilities and correct user licensing. Validate scope and entitlements.

manualCheck: If you configured long audit retention (years), verify the required premium audit licensing and any add-ons are assigned to users generating those events.

rules.title: Teams Rooms Basic over 25 rooms (requires Pro for additional rooms)

recommendation.textTemplate: TEAMS ROOMS LICENSING — Teams Rooms Basic is limited to 25 rooms; additional rooms require Teams Rooms Pro.

manualCheck: Count Teams Rooms Basic licenses assigned to rooms. If >25, additional rooms require Teams Rooms Pro.
Validate that Teams Rooms accounts are only assigned Teams Rooms Basic/Pro (not Teams Shared Device).

rules.title: Teams Shared Devices license assigned to Teams Rooms (not supported)

recommendation.textTemplate: TEAMS ROOMS LICENSING — Remove Teams Shared Devices licenses from Teams Rooms devices; assign Teams Rooms Basic/Pro instead.

manualCheck: Teams Rooms devices should only be licensed with Teams Rooms Basic/Pro. Teams Shared Devices licenses are not supported on Teams Rooms devices.

rules.title: Auto attendants / call queues missing Resource Account license

recommendation.textTemplate: TEAMS PHONE REVIEW — Resource accounts for Auto Attendants/Call Queues require a Teams Phone Resource Account license.

manualCheck: In Teams admin center: Voice > Resource accounts. Ensure each resource account has the 'Teams Phone Resource Account' license assigned.

rules.title: Teams Phone expected but users lack Teams Phone entitlement (manual check)

recommendation.textTemplate: TEAMS PHONE REVIEW — Validate Teams Phone licensing for voice-enabled users (Teams Phone is required before calling plans / PSTN usage).

manualCheck: Identify users enabled for voice (phone numbers, dial plans, calling policies). Confirm they have Teams Phone licensing per Microsoft guidance.

rules.title: Teams usage without desktop client might indicate frontline device profile (review)

recommendation.textTemplate: FRONTLINE REVIEW — Teams usage is web/mobile-only. Validate device profile and whether frontline licensing is appropriate.

rules.title: Users enrolled devices but lack Intune license (manual)

recommendation.textTemplate: NONCOMPLIANT — Devices are enrolled/managed but some users may lack Intune licensing. Validate and assign Intune licenses where needed.

manualCheck: In Intune: Devices > All devices (or Graph /deviceManagement/managedDevices). Map enrolled users to their Intune entitlements.
Microsoft guidance: users must have an Intune license assigned before enrolling devices.

rules.title: App protection policies (MAM) targeted to users without Intune entitlement (manual)

recommendation.textTemplate: NONCOMPLIANT — MAM policies targeted without ensuring users have Intune entitlement. Validate target users and assign licensing.

manualCheck: If Intune App Protection Policies are targeted to users, those users typically need Intune licensing even if they don't enroll devices.

rules.title: Power BI sharing/collaboration attempted by Free users

recommendation.textTemplate: NONCOMPLIANT — Power BI publishing/sharing requires Pro or PPU (unless Premium capacity covers viewing). Validate sharers/editors licensing.

manualCheck: Check Power BI workspaces: members/contributors without Pro/PPU is a licensing issue unless Premium capacity rules apply.
Creators/sharers generally require Pro or PPU.

rules.title: Power BI self-service trials/purchases create license sprawl

recommendation.textTemplate: REVIEW — Control Power BI self-service trials/purchases to reduce license sprawl and surprise costs.

manualCheck: In Power BI admin portal: tenant settings for trials/purchases. In M365 admin: review trial SKUs and self-service purchases.

rules.title: Unlicensed shared mailbox approaching 50 GB storage limit

recommendation.textTemplate: MAILBOX STORAGE WARNING — Unlicensed shared mailbox is approaching the 50 GB limit. Assign Exchange Online Plan 2 (100 GB + archive) or migrate data before mail flow stops.

rules.title: Inactive mailbox (free) — unlicensed on litigation hold, safely archived

recommendation.textTemplate: INACTIVE MAILBOX (FREE) — Unlicensed mailbox on Litigation Hold is safely archived as an Inactive Mailbox for eDiscovery at no cost. No action required for the mailbox. Check OneDrive for unprotected data.

rules.title: Unlicensed user with data at risk of purge

recommendation.textTemplate: UNLICENSED WITH DATA — Microsoft purges unlicensed mailbox and OneDrive data after 30 days. Back up, convert to Shared Mailbox, or re-license before data is lost.

rules.title: Disabled account on litigation hold retaining expensive license (E5 Data Hoarder / Inactive Hold)

recommendation.textTemplate: E5 DATA HOARDER / INACTIVE HOLD — Account is disabled but retains a license because of litigation hold. A license is not required to maintain a hold. The license can be safely removed — Microsoft will automatically convert this to a free Inactive Mailbox that retains all content and holds indefinitely.

rules.title: Disabled account review — EXO not connected, cannot verify hold status

recommendation.textTemplate: DISABLED ACCOUNT REVIEW — Sign-in is blocked. Cannot verify litigation hold status (EXO not connected). Check for active holds before removing license to avoid data loss.

rules.title: Disabled shared mailbox with MDO policy coverage — downgrade, do not remove

recommendation.textTemplate: DISABLED SHARED MAILBOX — Account is disabled and converted to shared mailbox, but in scope of MDO policies. Do NOT remove license entirely — downgrade to Exchange Online Plan 2 or add standalone Defender for Office 365 P1 add-on.

rules.title: Dormant admin risk — unlicensed admin account with no sign-in

recommendation.textTemplate: DORMANT ADMIN REVIEW — Unlicensed admin account has not signed in recently. Even without a license this is a security concern — dormant admin accounts are potential targets for compromise. Review whether the account should be disabled and audit for unauthorized activity.

rules.title: Automation account — unlicensed non-interactive service identity

recommendation.textTemplate: AUTOMATION ACCOUNT — Unlicensed service/sync account detected via non-interactive sign-in pattern. No license cost but verify that Conditional Access covers non-interactive flows. Consider converting to a Workload Identity.

rules.title: Non-human account holding premium user suite (resource/room/shared)

recommendation.textTemplate: NON-HUMAN ACCOUNT REVIEW — Non-human account is holding a premium user suite. Non-human accounts typically do not require productivity suites. If a license is needed (>50 GB or archive), consider using Exchange Online Plan 2 instead.

rules.title: Shared mailbox with MDO policy coverage — requires license for MDO

recommendation.textTemplate: SHARED MAILBOX — Under 50 GB but in scope of MDO policies. Downgrade to Exchange Online Plan 2 or add standalone Defender for Office 365 P1 add-on instead of full removal.

rules.title: Redundant archive add-on on Exchange Plan 2 shared mailbox

recommendation.textTemplate: REDUNDANT ARCHIVE — Shared mailbox has Exchange Plan 2 AND standalone Exchange Online Archiving. Plan 2 natively includes auto-expanding archives. The Archiving add-on can be safely removed.

rules.title: Admin account holding full productivity suite

recommendation.textTemplate: ADMIN — Admin accounts should use only Entra ID P2 and security SKUs, not full productivity suites. Use a separate daily-driver account for productivity.

rules.title: Entra ID P2 downgrade — standalone P2 with no PIM or risk-based CA need

recommendation.textTemplate: ENTRA P2 DOWNGRADE — Has standalone Entra ID P2 but is not an admin (no PIM required) and not in scope for risk-based CA. Downgrade to Entra ID P1 for standard MFA/CA.

rules.title: Duplicate review — likely redundant but unmapped SKUs present

recommendation.textTemplate: DUPLICATE REVIEW — Likely redundant with suite but user also has unmapped SKU(s). Validate coverage manually before removing.

rules.title: Exchange Kiosk candidate — EXO Plan 1 user with OWA-only and low storage

recommendation.textTemplate: EXCHANGE KIOSK CANDIDATE — Has Exchange Plan 1 but only accesses email via OWA with low storage. Downgrade to Exchange Kiosk to save cost.

rules.title: Suite inversion — E3 + add-ons exceed E5 cost

recommendation.textTemplate: SUITE INVERSION — E3 + E5-included add-ons cost more than full M365 E5. Upgrade to E5 to save money AND unlock remaining E5 capabilities.

rules.title: E5 consolidation — E3 + add-ons can simplify to single E5 SKU

recommendation.textTemplate: E5 CONSOLIDATION — E3 + add-ons can be simplified to 1 SKU (M365 E5) with full feature alignment. Not necessarily cheaper, but simplifies governance.

rules.title: Bundle consolidation — O365 E3 + EMS E3 + Windows E3 to M365 E3

recommendation.textTemplate: BUNDLE CONSOLIDATION — Separate O365 + EMS + Windows SKUs cost more than the equivalent M365 bundle. Consolidate to save and simplify.

rules.title: Teams unbundling — suite bundles Teams but zero Teams activity

recommendation.textTemplate: TEAMS UNBUNDLING — Suite bundles Teams but user shows 0 Teams activity. Switch to the equivalent Without Teams SKU to save on the bundled Teams component.

rules.title: Windows license review — standalone Windows SKU with no Windows activations

recommendation.textTemplate: WINDOWS LICENSE REVIEW — Standalone Windows subscription assigned but no Windows platform activations detected. Consider removing the Windows subscription.

rules.title: Premium add-on review — desktop app license but only mobile/web activations

recommendation.textTemplate: PREMIUM ADD-ON REVIEW — Desktop app license assigned but only mobile/web activations detected. Consider downgrading to a web-only SKU.

rules.title: Shelfware review — web-only product with no activity telemetry

recommendation.textTemplate: SHELFWARE REVIEW — Web-only product assigned but no app/SharePoint activity detected. Web-only products lack activation telemetry — verify actual browser usage before removing.

rules.title: Teams Phone entitlement without Teams client service plan

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — Teams Phone/Audio Conferencing entitlement detected but no Teams client (TEAMS1) service plan enabled. Add Teams add-on to activate telephony, or remove Teams Phone if not needed.

rules.title: Teams Phone review — Teams Phone without calling plan or PSTN route

recommendation.textTemplate: TEAMS PHONE REVIEW — Teams Phone SKU assigned but no Microsoft Calling Plan detected. If tenant uses Direct Routing or Operator Connect, the license is valid. If no PSTN route is configured, verify with the Teams administrator.

rules.title: Calling plan review — calling plan assigned but zero Teams calls

recommendation.textTemplate: CALLING PLAN REVIEW — Calling Plan assigned but 0 Teams calls recorded in the report period. Consider removing the calling plan and reallocating or cancelling the subscription.

rules.title: Teams Phone right-sizing — non-human account with Phone Standard instead of Shared Devices

recommendation.textTemplate: TEAMS PHONE RIGHT-SIZING — Non-human account has Teams Phone Standard but only needs Teams Shared Devices license for common area phones, lobby devices, or conference rooms.

rules.title: Copilot prerequisite missing — no qualifying base license

recommendation.textTemplate: COPILOT PREREQUISITE MISSING — Copilot assigned but no valid base license (E3/E5, Business Standard/Premium, or Education A3/A5). Copilot will not function. Assign a qualifying base license or reallocate the Copilot license.

rules.title: Copilot reclaim — zero Copilot activity (multiple paths)

recommendation.textTemplate: COPILOT RECLAIM — Copilot license assigned but zero Copilot activity detected. Reclaim and reallocate to maximize ROI.

rules.title: Copilot watchlist — zero Copilot activity but active in M365 workloads

recommendation.textTemplate: COPILOT WATCHLIST — Copilot assigned with zero Copilot activity, but user IS active in M365 workloads. Candidate for enablement/training before reclaiming.

rules.title: Copilot active — license in use, monitor adoption depth

recommendation.textTemplate: COPILOT ACTIVE — Copilot license assigned and active. Monitor adoption depth for ROI.

rules.title: Security Copilot — verify SOC/security analyst usage

recommendation.textTemplate: COPILOT — Microsoft Security Copilot assigned. Security Copilot is a SOC/security analyst tool billed by Security Compute Units. Verify this user actively uses Defender/Sentinel investigations.

rules.title: Copilot Studio — developer/admin tool for building chatbots

recommendation.textTemplate: COPILOT STUDIO — Studio license assigned. Verify developer/admin usage via Teams admin center, or reallocate if no sign-in activity.

rules.title: AI add-on overlap — Teams Premium redundant with Copilot

recommendation.textTemplate: AI ADD-ON OVERLAP — Has both Teams Premium and M365 Copilot. Copilot natively includes Teams Intelligent Recap. If user does not use Premium's advanced webinar/branding features, Teams Premium is redundant — remove it.

rules.title: AI overlap review — Teams Premium + Copilot but user organizes meetings

recommendation.textTemplate: AI OVERLAP REVIEW — Has both Teams Premium and M365 Copilot. User organizes meetings — verify whether Premium's advanced webinar branding or custom templates are needed before removing.

rules.title: Power BI Pro review — tenant has Premium Capacity, consumers may use Free

recommendation.textTemplate: POWER BI PRO REVIEW — Tenant has Power BI Premium Capacity or user has PPU. Verify user's role (creator vs consumer) before downgrading or removing Pro.

rules.title: EXO Plan 2 downgrade — mailbox under 50 GB with low usage

recommendation.textTemplate: EXO PLAN 2 DOWNGRADE — Exchange Plan 2 assigned but mailbox is under 50 GB and usage is not high. Plan 1 may suffice.

rules.title: EXO Plan 2 review — missing mailbox data for downgrade assessment

recommendation.textTemplate: EXO PLAN 2 REVIEW — Exchange Plan 2 assigned but mailbox size and/or activity data is missing. Validate size and hold requirements before considering downgrade to Plan 1.

rules.title: OneDrive Plan 2 review — unlimited storage but low usage

recommendation.textTemplate: ONEDRIVE PLAN 2 REVIEW — OneDrive Plan 2 (unlimited) assigned but low usage. Consider downgrading to OneDrive Plan 1 (1 TB) to save cost.

rules.title: Frontline review — missing platform data prevents right-sizing

recommendation.textTemplate: FRONTLINE REVIEW — Premium suite assigned but M365 app platform usage data is missing. Cannot safely determine desktop app dependency for right-sizing to F1/F3.

rules.title: Frontline blocked — archive mailbox prevents F3 downgrade

recommendation.textTemplate: FRONTLINE BLOCKED — User only uses web/mobile apps but has an active archive mailbox or desktop activations. F3 downgrade would destroy archive data or deactivate Office on PCs. Migrate archive or consolidate devices first.

rules.title: Frontline rescue — F3 blocked but E1/Business Basic is viable

recommendation.textTemplate: FRONTLINE RESCUE — F3 is blocked but user only uses web/mobile. Downgrade to E1 or Business Basic which supports 50 GB mailbox + unlimited archive.

rules.title: F3 to F1 downgrade — F3 user with zero email/OneDrive activity

recommendation.textTemplate: F3 TO F1 DOWNGRADE — F3 user with 0 email and 0 OneDrive activity. Downgrade to M365 F1 to save cost.

rules.title: Frontline desktop compliance violation — F-series with desktop activations

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — F-series SKU does NOT include desktop Office apps, but desktop activations detected. This is a licensing compliance violation. Upgrade to E3/Business Premium or remove desktop installations.

rules.title: Frontline add-on bloat — F-series + add-ons exceed E3/Business Premium

recommendation.textTemplate: FRONTLINE ADD-ON BLOAT — F-series base plus add-ons totals meet or exceed E3/Business Premium. Upgrade to eliminate F-series restrictions and consolidate into 1 SKU.

rules.title: Defender suite upsell — partial Defender coverage

recommendation.textTemplate: DEFENDER SUITE UPSELL — User has partial Defender coverage. Add Microsoft Defender Suite for Business or Microsoft Defender Suite add-on for comprehensive protection.

rules.title: Purview upsell — no advanced compliance coverage

recommendation.textTemplate: PURVIEW UPSELL — No advanced compliance coverage detected. Consider Microsoft Purview add-ons for DLP, Information Protection, Insider Risk Management, and eDiscovery.

rules.title: High risk sharing — external file sharing without advanced compliance

recommendation.textTemplate: HIGH RISK SHARING — User shared files externally but lacks advanced compliance coverage (DLP/Information Protection). High priority for Purview add-on or E5 step-up.

rules.title: Entra Suite overlap — standalone Governance add-on redundant with Entra Suite

recommendation.textTemplate: ENTRA SUITE OVERLAP — Entra Suite natively includes Entra ID P2 and Governance. Remove standalone Governance add-on(s).

rules.title: Bundle consolidation — Entra ID P2 + Governance to Entra Suite

recommendation.textTemplate: BUNDLE CONSOLIDATION — Entra ID P2 + Governance is more expensive than Entra Suite. Consolidate to Entra Suite to save and gain Internet/Private Access.

rules.title: Intune Suite overlap — standalone add-ons now included in M365 E3/E5

recommendation.textTemplate: INTUNE SUITE OVERLAP — Standalone Intune add-ons (Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, Endpoint Privilege Management) assigned alongside M365 E3/E5. Microsoft rolled these into E3/E5 in late 2025. Consider removing the standalone add-on(s).

rules.title: Licensing check — Entra Suite with E3/E5 consolidation opportunity

recommendation.textTemplate: LICENSING CHECK — Entra Suite present. For E3/E5 users, validate whether consolidating into M365 E5 plus a smaller Entra footprint would be cheaper.

rules.title: Intune review — standalone Intune/EMS with zero enrolled devices

recommendation.textTemplate: INTUNE REVIEW — Standalone Intune/EMS license assigned but 0 enrolled devices in Intune. The MDM/MAM capability is entirely unused. Consider removing the standalone Intune/EMS license or enrolling devices.

rules.title: Intune review — standalone Intune but 100% web-only access

recommendation.textTemplate: INTUNE REVIEW — Standalone Intune/EMS license with 100% web-only access. Intune device/app management is unutilized. Consider removing the standalone Intune/EMS license or enrolling devices. If security is required for web access, Entra ID P1 alone may be sufficient.

rules.title: Cloud license sync error — assignment synchronization failure

recommendation.textTemplate: CLOUD LICENSE SYNC ERROR — License assignment synchronization failed. Check Cloud Licensing allotment assignments in Entra ID.

rules.title: Business Basic review — missing platform data prevents downgrade assessment

recommendation.textTemplate: BUSINESS BASIC REVIEW — Business Standard assigned but M365 app platform usage data is missing. Validate desktop app dependency before downgrading to Business Basic.

rules.title: Business Basic candidate — Business Standard user with web/mobile only

recommendation.textTemplate: BUSINESS BASIC CANDIDATE — Business Standard user only uses web/mobile apps (no desktop). Downgrade to Business Basic to save cost.

rules.title: E1 downgrade candidate — O365 E1 replaceable by Business Basic (under 300 seats)

recommendation.textTemplate: E1 DOWNGRADE CANDIDATE — O365 E1 assigned but tenant is under the 300-seat Business cap. Downgrade to M365 Business Basic for identical web/mobile capabilities at lower cost.

rules.title: O365 E3 to E1 — web/mobile only user with small mailbox

recommendation.textTemplate: O365 E3 TO E1 — Office 365 E3 user with web/mobile only access and mailbox under 50 GB. Downgrade to Office 365 E1.

rules.title: E3 to Business Premium — under 300 seats with small mailbox

recommendation.textTemplate: E3 TO BUSINESS PREMIUM — M365 E3 user in a tenant with spare Business-tier capacity and mailbox under 50 GB. Downgrade to M365 Business Premium for same apps + better endpoint security at lower cost.

rules.title: Business Premium inversion — Standard + add-ons exceed Business Premium

recommendation.textTemplate: BUSINESS PREMIUM INVERSION — Business Standard + security add-ons costs more than Business Premium. Upgrade to Business Premium which natively includes Intune, Entra ID P1, and Defender for Business.

rules.title: Business Premium security review — Defender Suite overlap assessment

recommendation.textTemplate: BUSINESS PREMIUM SECURITY REVIEW — Business Premium already includes Defender for Business and MDO P1. Verify the Defender Suite for Business add-on capabilities (MDI, Defender for Cloud Apps, Entra ID P2, MDO P2) are actively used to justify the cost.

rules.title: E5 voice review — E5 user with zero meetings and calls

recommendation.textTemplate: E5 VOICE REVIEW — E5 user with 0 meetings organized and 0 Teams calls. Consider swapping to the equivalent Without PSTN SKU to remove unused telecom costs.

rules.title: App arbitrage — Apps for Enterprise replaceable by Apps for Business (under 300 seats)

recommendation.textTemplate: APP ARBITRAGE — Apps for Enterprise assigned but tenant has spare Business-tier capacity. Downgrade to Apps for Business for identical desktop applications at lower cost.

rules.title: PBI PPU overlap — full PPU when base suite already includes Pro

recommendation.textTemplate: PBI PPU OVERLAP — Full Power BI Premium Per User assigned but base suite already includes Power BI Pro. Consider swapping to the PPU Add-On which layers Premium features on top of the included Pro.

rules.title: Standalone apps review — desktop app license with web/mobile only usage

recommendation.textTemplate: STANDALONE APPS REVIEW — Standalone desktop app license assigned but user only uses web/mobile. Consider downgrading to Business Basic or F3 if no desktop dependency exists.

rules.title: Bundle opportunity — Exchange Kiosk/Plan 1 + standalone apps consolidation

recommendation.textTemplate: BUNDLE OPPORTUNITY — Exchange Kiosk/Plan 1 + standalone apps costs more than M365 Business Standard. Consider consolidating into a single SKU to save and upgrade mailbox capacity.

rules.title: Bundle inefficiency — Business Basic + Apps for Business to Business Standard

recommendation.textTemplate: BUNDLE INEFFICIENCY — Business Basic + Apps for Business costs more than M365 Business Standard which natively includes both. Consolidate to save.

rules.title: Forwarding mailbox review — mailbox exists only to forward email

recommendation.textTemplate: FORWARDING MAILBOX REVIEW — Mailbox auto-forwards all mail with no interactive sign-in. Consider converting to a free Mail Contact, shared mailbox, or Exchange transport rule.

rules.title: Forwarding mailbox review — forward-only with low activity

recommendation.textTemplate: FORWARDING MAILBOX REVIEW — Mailbox forwards all mail (no local delivery) with low exchange activity. Consider converting to a free Mail Contact or shared mailbox.

rules.title: Expensive cold storage — zero activity but significant stored data

recommendation.textTemplate: EXPENSIVE COLD STORAGE — 0 activity but significant data stored. Consider converting the mailbox to Shared/Inactive, migrating OneDrive to a SharePoint Archive site, and removing the license.

rules.title: Background sync only — zero interactive activity but OneDrive syncing

recommendation.textTemplate: BACKGROUND SYNC ONLY — Zero interactive M365 activity but OneDrive synced files in the background. This usually indicates an abandoned, powered-on device. Investigate device status and consider license removal.

rules.title: Dormant Cloud PC — zero connected hours and no recent sign-in

recommendation.textTemplate: DORMANT CLOUD PC — {cpcSkuFriendly} shows 0 connected hours in the last 90 days and user has no recent sign-in activity. Review Cloud PC utilization and consider reclaiming the license. Annual cost: {annualCostEUR}

rules.title: Cloud PC review — zero connected hours but user has recent sign-in activity

recommendation.textTemplate: CLOUD PC REVIEW — {cpcSkuFriendly} shows 0 connected hours in the last 90 days, but user has recent sign-in activity. Verify whether the Cloud PC is still needed. Annual cost: {annualCostEUR}

rules.title: Low utilization Cloud PC — under 10 connected hours in 90 days

recommendation.textTemplate: CLOUD PC REVIEW — {cpcSkuFriendly} shows only {cpcTotalHours} connected hours in the last 90 days. Review Cloud PC utilization and consider downsizing to a lower spec or reclaiming. Annual cost: {annualCostEUR}

rules.title: Cloud PC assigned but no usage data available — cross-check with sign-in logs

recommendation.textTemplate: CLOUD PC REVIEW — {cpcSkuFriendly} assigned but no Cloud PC usage data available. Cross-check with sign-in activity to determine whether the Cloud PC is actively used. Annual cost: {annualCostEUR}

rules.title: Cloud PC SKUs purchased but no devices provisioned

recommendation.textTemplate: CLOUD PC REVIEW — Cloud PC SKUs are purchased in the tenant but no Cloud PCs are provisioned. Verify whether deployment is planned or the licenses should be deallocated to reduce waste.

rules.title: Cloud PC right-sizing audit — verify tier matches workload requirements

recommendation.textTemplate: CLOUD PC RIGHT-SIZING — Review whether the assigned Cloud PC tiers (vCPU/RAM/Storage) match the actual workload requirements for each user. Over-provisioned Cloud PCs waste budget; under-provisioned ones degrade performance.

manualCheck: In Intune admin center: Devices > Windows 365 > All Cloud PCs, review the assigned service plan tier for each user.
Cross-reference with the Cloud PC Total Hours (90d) and Cloud PC Type columns in the LOA output CSV.
For users with 8vCPU/32GB Cloud PCs showing < 20 hours/90 days, consider downgrading to 4vCPU/16GB or 2vCPU/8GB.
For users consistently using > 80% of allotted hours, consider upgrading to ensure adequate performance.
Review provisioning policies to ensure new Cloud PCs default to the minimum viable tier.
